info.title: M.A.R.C.U.S. Public API
info.summary: Programmatic access to a customer's AV fleet.
info.description:
Read-only integration API for the M.A.R.C.U.S. monitoring platform. Use it to sync device inventory into a CMDB, mirror alerts into an incident tool, or feed dashboards with live fleet state. Every route is scoped to the token's tenant — one token, one customer's data.

Polling once a minute is ample for most use cases. Cursor-based pagination keeps list endpoints stable under concurrent inserts.

tags.name: Meta
tags.description: Health and identity of the calling token.

tags.name: Devices
tags.description: AV endpoints under management — displays, cameras, DSPs, control processors.

tags.name: Firmware
tags.description: Firmware versions across the fleet, against the targets set on the Firmware page. Needs the view.firmware scope.

tags.name: Assets
tags.description: The CMDB inventory — every physical thing the tenant owns, monitored or not. Broader than Devices: includes mounts, cables, spares, retired gear.

tags.name: Alerts
tags.description: Open + historical incidents raised on devices and collectors.

tags.name: Events
tags.description: Device-emitted events — state changes, adapter messages, telemetry deltas.

tags.name: Audit
tags.description: The tenant's audit trail of changes and commands. Needs the view.audit scope.

tags.name: Room Readiness
tags.description: Results of each room's power schedule (switched off at night, on in the morning) and readiness checks (a test routine, down to every step). Needs the nightly.view scope.

get.description: Returns the tenant id, token name, and granted scopes. Useful for smoke-testing that your bearer header is set correctly and that the token targets the tenant you expect.
Every device visible to the token, ordered by most-recently-seen. Supports building / room / status filters and cursor pagination.

parameters.name: status
parameters.description: Exact match on latest known status.

parameters.name: firmware_status
parameters.description: Only devices whose firmware has this status against its target. `differs_from_target` lists the devices to update.

get.description: Full device record including the latest metrics snapshot. Use this after resolving an id from an event, alert, or CMDB record.
The most recent telemetry snapshot the collector produced for the device. Metrics shape is adapter-dependent — see your adapter reference for keys.
Cursor-paginated event feed for one device, most recent first.

The fleet's firmware: one row per make, model and firmware version, with how many devices run it and how it compares with the target set on the Firmware page. Use `firmware_status=differs_from_target` for what needs updating, then `GET /pub/v1/devices?firmware_status=differs_from_target` for the devices themselves. Requires the `view.firmware` scope.

parameters.name: firmware_status
parameters.description: Only versions with this status against their target.

200.description: Firmware versions, by make and model, most used first.

get.description: Every building in the tenant, alphabetically. Includes address, timezone, optional coordinates, and location + region names.
Every room in the tenant, optionally filtered by parent building. Each row carries the building id + name so a picker or sync task doesn't need to join.

Every asset in the tenant's CMDB. Broader than /devices — an asset may or may not be monitored. Use the `monitored` filter to slice one way or the other; combined with the `device_id` field on each row, an integrator can sync inventory into a CMDB and cross-reference the live device state without a second call.

parameters.name: category
parameters.description: Exact match (display, camera, audio, mount, cable, remote, …).

parameters.name: status
parameters.description: Exact match.

parameters.name: monitored
parameters.description: true → only assets linked to a monitored device row; false → only unmonitored inventory. Omit to see everything.

get.description: Single asset by id. Same shape as the list entry — no additional fields on the detail view.
Alerts raised on devices or collectors, most recent first. Filter by status and severity to sync only open critical incidents into your on-call tool.

parameters.name: status
parameters.description: Exact match.

parameters.name: severity
parameters.description: Exact match.

get.description: Cross-fleet event stream, most recent first. Filter by device_id to narrow, or omit the filter to poll every device the token can see.

The tenant's audit trail, most recent first: who changed what, and when, with before/after snapshots of the record. Use it to feed a SIEM or keep a change record outside the platform. Secrets such as device credentials and password or token hashes are never recorded. Requires the `view.audit` scope.

parameters.name: action
parameters.description: Exact action, e.g. `device.update`. End with a dot (`device.`) to match every action on that kind of record.

parameters.name: target_kind
parameters.description: Exact kind of record, e.g. `device`, `user`, `notification_channel`.

parameters.name: target_id
parameters.description: Matches the primary or the related target, so a device's feed also includes commands sent to it.

parameters.name: actor
parameters.description: Exact actor label, as shown in `actor`.

parameters.name: device_id
parameters.description: Entries about this device, including commands sent to it.

parameters.name: room_id
parameters.description: Entries about this room and everything in it: its devices and their commands, its assets, and its Room Readiness runs.

parameters.name: building_id
parameters.description: Entries about this building, its rooms and everything in them.

parameters.name: location_id
parameters.description: Entries about this location (site), its buildings, rooms and everything in them. Place filters use each record's current place, so a device moved to another room appears under its new room, history included.

parameters.name: since
parameters.description: Entries at or after this time (RFC 3339). Use `since` or `last`, not both.

parameters.name: until
parameters.description: Entries before this time (RFC 3339).

parameters.name: last
parameters.description: A rolling window instead of `since`: `15m`, `2h`, `7d`, up to `366d`. For example `last=15m` returns the last 15 minutes.

get.summary: List rooms with their latest runs
get.description: Every room with its readiness check (the routine, its own or the customer default, and when it runs) and its latest power and readiness runs, so one call answers "is every room ready this morning?". A latest run is null for a room that hasn't had one. Not paginated. Requires the `nightly.view` scope.

200.description: Rooms, ordered by building then room.

get.description: Runs, most recent first: power runs (the room switched off and back on) and readiness runs (a test routine), each with a count of passed and failed steps. Fetch a run by id for the individual steps. Requires the `nightly.view` scope.

parameters.name: kind
parameters.description: `power` or `readiness`. Both when omitted.

parameters.name: status
parameters.description: One or more statuses, comma-separated, e.g. `failed` or `succeeded,failed`.

parameters.name: since
parameters.description: Runs scheduled at or after this time (RFC 3339).

parameters.name: until
parameters.description: Runs scheduled before this time (RFC 3339).

get.summary: Get a run with its steps
get.description: One run with every step of its test routine, in order: what was checked, on which device, what was expected and what was found. Requires the `nightly.view` scope.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: Run id (UUID).

bearerAuth.description: Mint a token from the portal at Settings → API tokens. Send it as `Authorization: Bearer avb_...` on every request. Query-string tokens are NOT accepted — the URL ends up in access logs.

Cursor.name: cursor
Cursor.description: Opaque pagination cursor from a previous response's `next_cursor`. Omit on the first call. Treat this as an opaque string — its shape may change.

BadRequest.description: Malformed request — invalid JSON, unknown filter value, or corrupt cursor.

Unauthorized.description: Missing, malformed, revoked, or expired bearer token.

Forbidden.description: Token authenticated but doesn't hold the scope this endpoint requires.

NotFound.description: Resource missing or invisible to this token.

message.description: Human-readable summary. Not intended for parsing.

next_cursor.description: Pass this back as `?cursor=` on the next call. `null` means this page is the last one.

name.description: The device's display name. Falls back to the adapter's reported id when no override is set in the portal.

protocol.description: The adapter the Collector uses for the device, e.g. `sony_bravia`, `tesira`, `cisco_roomos`, `aten_pdu`.

status.description: `unknown` when the device's Collector isn't reporting; `switched_off` while Room Readiness has it switched off for the night.

firmware_version.description: The device's firmware, as on the Firmware page: a `firmware_version` tag set in the portal, otherwise what the device last reported.

target_firmware_version.description: The target firmware set for the device's make and model on the Firmware page. Absent when none is set.

firmware_status.description: How the firmware compares with the target set for the device's make and model on the Firmware page: `matches_target`, `differs_from_target`, `no_target` (no target set) or `not_reported` (the device hasn't reported firmware).

metrics.description: Adapter-specific latest-known metrics. Shape varies by adapter.

category.description: Free-text with an application-layer allowlist (display, camera, audio, conferencing, control_panel, touch_panel, cable, mount, rack, remote, microphone, speaker, projector, screen, computer, furniture, storage, other).

room_id.description: Absent when the asset is unplaced (in-storage / decommissioned).

monitored.description: True when a monitored device row is linked to this asset. See `device_id` for the pairing.

device_id.description: The paired device id when `monitored` is true — use it against /pub/v1/devices/{id} for live telemetry.

subject_kind.description: What the alert is about. `room` alerts come from Room Readiness: a failed health check (`readiness_failed`) or power cycle (`power_cycle_failed`).

alert_key.description: Stable identifier for the rule that fired, e.g. `device.offline`, `collector.stale`.

id.description: Event id: a number, sent as a string. Increases over time.

actor.description: Who made the change: a user, an API token, or `system:` / `auto:` for platform actions.

related_target_kind.description: A second record the action affected, e.g. the device a command was sent to.

before.description: The record before the change, where applicable.

after.description: The record after the change, where applicable.

kind.description: `power`: the room switched off at night and back on. `readiness`: a test routine.

routine_id.description: The test routine the run used; null for a power-cycle-only run.

phase.description: How far the run got. `ready` means the room passed.

started_at.description: When the run began: the evening power-off, or the start of a run without a power cycle.

powered_on_at.description: When the morning power-on began; null until then, and for runs without a power cycle.

duration_seconds.description: How long the room took to be ready (or to fail) after power-on; for a run without a power cycle, from its start.

steps_total.description: Steps recorded so far, including the scheduled power off and power on.

index.description: Position in the routine, from 0. The scheduled power off and power on come first, as -2 and -1.

device_id.description: Null for steps that aren't about one device.

expected.description: What the step checked for, as configured in the routine.

readings.description: Check steps only: for each device judged, where its reading came from. `fresh` is a poll made for the step; `last_report` is the device's last regular report (an ATEN PDU, or a fresh poll that didn't come back within 60 seconds); `none` means there was no reading. Null for other steps and for runs before readings were recorded.

age_s.description: How old the reading was when the step judged it, in seconds.

make.description: Empty when the devices haven't reported one.

firmware_version.description: Empty for devices that haven't reported firmware.

target_firmware_version.description: The target set for this make and model. Absent when none is set.

firmware_status.description: How the firmware compares with the target set for the device's make and model on the Firmware page: `matches_target`, `differs_from_target`, `no_target` (no target set) or `not_reported` (the device hasn't reported firmware).

device_count.description: Devices of this make and model on this firmware.

routine_id.description: The room's readiness routine (its own, or the customer default); null when the room isn't checked.

readiness_time.description: When the readiness check runs, HH:MM in the customer's timezone; null when the room isn't checked.

excluded_until.description: The room is left out of both the power schedule and readiness checks up to and including this date.

latest_run.description: The more recent of the two below.
